div.l: But of his craft fro Berwyk in to ware
Ne was ther swich an nother ꝑpardoner
For in his male he hadde a pylewber
Swich þat he seyd was our lady veylle
He sayde he hadde a gobet of þe seylle
That seynt Petir hadde when þat he wente
Vppon þe see til Ihu crist hym hente
He hadde a Croys of latoıı̄un ful of stones
And in a glas he hadde pigges bones
But wit þeise relikes whan that he fonde
A poure ꝑparson dwelling vppon londe
Vppon a day he gat him more moneye
Than þat þe ꝑparson gat in monethes tweye
And þus wit feyned flatering and Iapes
He made the ꝑparson ⁊and þe peple his Apes
But trewely to tellen atte þe laste
He was in churche a noble Ecciaste
Wel couthe he rede a lesson or a story
But alderbeste he song an offetory
For wel he wiste whan þat song was songe
He moste preche and welle affile his tonge
To wynne seluyr as he wel kowde
Therfore he songe so meriely ⁊and lowde
¶ Now haue I tolde yow sotheli in a clause
The estat / the array þe nombre ⁊and ek þe cause
Whi þat assembled was þis companye
In suthwerk at þis gentil hosterye
That highte the Tabbard faste bi þe belle
But now is tyme yow for to telle
How that we beryn vs þat ylke nyght
Whan we were in that Osterye a lyght
And after wol y tellen of oure viage
And alle þe remenant of our pilgⁱmage
But ferst y pray yow of yowre curtesie
That ye ne rette it noght my vilenye
Thow that I pleynelye speke in þis mater
To telle ȝow here wordes and here chere
Ne though I. speke her wordes ꝓpropurly
For this ye knowen as wel as I .
Who so schall tellen a tale aft̉er a man
He moot reherse as neygh as eủere he ca
